data.narrative:
Monaire is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Nishant Kanapilly and Rahul Subramany, having raised $4.1M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a fragmented comp universe of 8 private peers in Climate & Energy (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix) plus 1 public comparable (LNZA), though cross-stage heterogeneity limits their direct applicability.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using the $4.1M in total capital raised as a baseline proxy, a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $10M. The peer-median approach was not deployable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy peer set—while 8 sector peers exist, none met the threshold of 3+ datapoints at matching stage or valuation tier needed for a robust median calculation.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $9M (low) to $12M (high), centered on a $10M median. This single-method result carries material uncertainty: the estimate hinges on (1) the appropriateness of the 2.5x Seed multiplier for Monaire specifically, (2) the proxy assumption that total raised approximates pre-money valuation, and (3) the absence of granular peer benchmarking. Additional uncertainty stems from the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of climate tech and the heterogeneity of peer maturity and technology focus. A subsequent financing event or closer peer comparability would sharpen this range materially.
